s1.where: A mostly empty white screen with a writing box at the bottom saying 'Ask ChatGPT' and three suggestions above it.
s1.expectation: I believe this is the starting page, where one begins a conversation with the machine. But that is a deduction, not something I was told.
s1.cue: The box at the bottom that says 'Ask ChatGPT', and the three lines 'Start a voice chat', 'Create an image or sticker', 'Write or edit'. There is no heading at all; the only words at the top are 'Get Plus', which is an advertisement, not a place.

first_pass.why: Nothing on this screen names it. If the telephone rang and I came back, I would see a blank page and have to reason out from the writing box what I was doing. 'Get Plus' at the top tells me nothing about where I am.
first_pass.solution: A plain heading at the top, such as 'New conversation' or 'Home', in the place where 'Get Plus' now sits.

test_cases.action: Open the app on your phone (if something else is showing, press the round-arrow home/back only as described below). Before tapping anything, say where you are and what told you. Then tap the three-line button at the top left, tap 'Library', come back with the arrow at the top left, and — if the side panel is showing — tap the dimmed area on the right to close it. Say again where you are.
test_cases.real_if: it is real if, both times, nothing on the page lets you name where you are
test_cases.not_real_if: it is not real if something on the page lets you name it
test_cases.what_happened: I opened the app. It came up on the first page with the keyboard already open. At the top there were only the three-line button, 'Get Plus' and a round symbol on the right; below were 'Create an image or sticker', 'Write or edit' and the box 'Ask ChatGPT'. Nothing named the page. I could only guess from 'Ask ChatGPT' that this is where one starts. I opened the side panel, tapped 'Library' (it said 'Library' at the top, which was reassuring), came back with the arrow, which reopened the side panel, and closed that by tapping the grey area on the right. I was back on the same blank page, and again nothing on it told me its name. Both times I had to work it out.

s1.closing_comment: Twice I looked at the first page, and twice nothing on it named where I was. I must still work it out from the writing box.

s2.where: A grey box in the middle of a darkened screen, asking me to enable the microphone, with 'Cancel' and 'Open settings'.
s2.expectation: Something has interrupted me to say the microphone is switched off, and it wants to send me to the telephone's settings.
s2.cue: The sentence 'Please enable microphone access in System Settings to use Voice.' There is no heading on the box; I had to read the whole paragraph.

first_pass.why: I can work it out by reading, but the box has no title. It warns me I will be sent away to 'Android settings' and must 'return to ChatGPT to continue' — that is exactly the sort of thing I would forget halfway through, and nothing here would remind me when I came back.
first_pass.solution: A short heading on the box, such as 'Microphone is switched off', and no instruction that relies on me remembering to come back.

test_cases.action: (Not run: the entry that opened that box is no longer on the app's first page, and reaching it another way would mean starting voice, which is not allowed.)
test_cases.reason_not_run: The test engineer told me the way into the microphone message is no longer on the first page, and reaching it otherwise would mean starting voice, which is not allowed on this phone.

s2.closing_comment: I could not try this one, so my view stands as it was: the box needs a heading of its own.

s3.where: A page of pictures — a flower, a woman in a denim jacket, stickers, a cartoon — with 'Trending' and 'Templates' at the top.
s3.expectation: Some sort of gallery of picture styles. I suppose it is for making pictures, because the box at the bottom says 'Create image'.
s3.cue: The box marked around 'Trending' and 'Templates', with 'Trending' shaded. And 'Create image' at the bottom.

first_pass.why: 'Trending' and 'Templates' are not names of a place; they are sorting words, and 'Trending' in particular is a fashionable term I would have to learn. Nothing at the top says 'Pictures' or 'Make a picture'. I only guessed from the words in the box at the very bottom.
first_pass.solution: A heading above the two tabs that says in plain words what this page is, such as 'Make a picture'.

test_cases.action: Tap the three-line button at the top left, then 'Images'. Before scrolling, say where you are and what told you. Then scroll the pictures down a little, stop, and — without scrolling back — say where you are now.
test_cases.real_if: it is real if, after the small scroll, nothing on screen lets you name the page
test_cases.not_real_if: it is not real if you can still name it from what you see
test_cases.what_happened: I opened the side panel and tapped 'Images'. The page that opened had the faint grey message 'Your generated images moved to Library' printed over the back arrow at the very top, then 'Trending' and 'Templates', then the pictures. Before scrolling, I could not see a page name. I only knew it was the pictures page because I had just tapped 'Images'. I scrolled down a little. 'Trending' and 'Templates' went off the top, and all that was left was pictures ('Sketch', 'Stickers', ''80s flashback') and 'Describe an image' at the bottom. Nothing named the page. Then, when I scrolled all the way back up to start the next test, I saw something I had not seen before: a proper heading 'Images' at the top beside the back arrow, with the message sitting neatly in a card below it. So the page does have a name. It was out of sight when the page first opened, and it goes again as soon as I scroll.

s3.closing_comment: The page is in fact called 'Images', which is a word I know. But that name was out of sight when the page opened and went again the moment I scrolled, so I still spent most of my time on it without a name.

s4.where: The same empty start page, but the suggestions at the bottom now sit under the words 'Write or edit', with a cross beside them.
s4.expectation: I have chosen 'Write or edit', and it is offering me ways to improve some writing — 'Improve flow', 'Rewrite for clarity', 'Turn ideas into an outline'.
s4.cue: The words 'Write or edit' in bold above the list, in the marked box. The writing box also says 'Write anything'.

first_pass.why: 'Write or edit' is plain English and it sits right above the choices it belongs to. If I looked away, it would remind me what I had chosen.

s5.where: A page headed 'ChatGPT Plus' with a table comparing 'Free' and 'Plus', and a large black button 'Upgrade for $19.99'.
s5.expectation: This is a page trying to sell me a paid subscription called Plus.
s5.cue: The large heading 'ChatGPT Plus', the price on the black button, and 'Renews monthly. Cancel anytime.'

first_pass.why: The heading is large and at the top, and together with the price it is perfectly clear that this is a subscription offer. I do not need to know what 'Plus' includes to know where I am.

s6.where: A page headed 'ChatGPT Go', with a comparison table and 'Upgrade for $8.00'.
s6.expectation: Another subscription offer, a cheaper one, called 'Go'.
s6.cue: The heading 'ChatGPT Go', the price, and 'Renews monthly'. The two buttons 'Go' and 'Plus' under the heading.

first_pass.why: 'Go' is not a name I recognise; to me 'Go' is an instruction, like a button to press. Reading the heading, I would think I was being told to go somewhere. It is the price further down that tells me what this is. I also notice the grey shading has moved from 'Plus' to 'Go', and I would not remember from the last page which shade meant 'chosen'.
first_pass.solution: Name the plan in ordinary words, for instance 'Basic paid plan', and mark the chosen option with a tick or the word 'Selected' rather than a change of grey.

test_cases.action: On the app's first page tap 'Get Plus' at the top. Say where you are. Tap 'Go' on the two-part switch, and say where you are now and which half of the switch is the chosen one. Then leave with the arrow at the top left. Do NOT tap any 'Upgrade' or 'Restore' button.
test_cases.real_if: it is real if you cannot tell which plan page you are on or which option is chosen
test_cases.not_real_if: it is not real if you can tell both
test_cases.what_happened: I tapped 'Get Plus'. The page said 'ChatGPT Plus' in large letters, with a two-part switch 'Go' | 'Plus' underneath and 'Upgrade for $19.99'. I knew I was on a page offering me a paid plan called Plus. I tapped 'Go'. The heading changed to 'ChatGPT Go' and the price to $8.00, so I could tell which plan page I was on by matching the heading to the switch. The chosen half is shaded grey, but its word is printed in a paler grey, while the half that is not chosen has its word in bold black. I would naturally have read the bold black one as the one that is 'on'; I only knew better because the heading said 'Go'. I left with the arrow without touching 'Upgrade' or 'Restore'.

s6.closing_comment: Tapping 'Go' changed the heading to 'ChatGPT Go', so I could tell which plan page I was on. The switch still shows the chosen half in pale grey and the other in bold black, which I would read the wrong way round without the heading.

s7.where: A mostly empty screen with 'Temporary chat' in the middle and 'This chat won't appear in history.'
s7.expectation: I am in a conversation that will not be saved.
s7.cue: The words 'Temporary chat' in the middle of the screen, which also appear in the writing box at the bottom.

first_pass.why: It says plainly what this is, twice, and the line underneath explains it. It is in the middle of the page rather than the top, but it is large and I cannot miss it.

s8.where: A panel risen from the bottom, headed 'Temporary chat settings', with 'Personalized' and 'Unpersonalized' choices and a 'Done' button.
s8.expectation: I am choosing the settings for the temporary conversation.
s8.cue: The heading 'Temporary chat settings' at the top of the panel.

first_pass.why: The panel has a clear heading of its own, which is exactly what I need when something pops up. If I looked away I would know what I was doing when I looked back.

s9.where: A menu drawn over the left side of the screen, headed 'ChatGPT', listing 'Images', 'Library', 'Projects', 'Scheduled', 'Plugins' and then a list of earlier items.
s9.expectation: This is the main menu of the program, where I can go to its different sections.
s9.cue: The list of section names with small pictures beside them. The heading only says 'ChatGPT', which is the name of the program.

first_pass.why: The heading is merely the name of the program, which I already know. None of the five entries is highlighted, so it does not tell me which of them I came from. I can see it is a menu, but it does not tell me where I am.
first_pass.solution: A heading such as 'Menu', and the section I am currently in marked clearly, perhaps in colour with the word 'You are here'.

test_cases.action: From the app's first page tap the three-line button at the top left. Say which part of the app you are in right now. Tap 'Library'; then tap the arrow at the top left to come back — the side panel opens again. Look at it: does anything on it show you where you just were? Then tap a conversation name in the list below the line, and open the side panel again: does anything show where you are now? Close it by tapping the dimmed area on the right.
test_cases.real_if: it is real if nothing on the side panel ever marks where you are
test_cases.not_real_if: it is not real if the side panel marks where you are or were
test_cases.what_happened: From the first page I opened the side panel. It said 'ChatGPT' at the top and listed 'Images', 'Library', 'Projects', 'Scheduled', 'Plugins'. Nothing was marked, so it did not tell me I had come from the first page. I tapped 'Library', then the arrow, and the side panel came back exactly as before: 'Library' was not marked in any way, so nothing reminded me where I had just been. (The same happened later after I visited 'Images'.) Then I tapped the conversation 'Hello Greeting' in the lower list, and later opened the side panel again. This time 'Hello Greeting' had a pale grey band behind it. So the panel does mark which conversation I am in, faintly. It never marks which section I have been in.

s9.closing_comment: The side panel does shade the conversation I am in, faintly, which I did not know. But it never marked 'Library' or 'Images' after I had been there, and its heading is still only the program's name.

s10.where: A white panel covering the bottom two-thirds of the picture page, with a cross, three small symbols in the middle, a curved arrow, a slider on the left and a row of coloured dots at the bottom.
s10.expectation: I think this may be for drawing, because of the pencil symbol and the coloured dots. But I am not at all sure.
s10.cue: The pencil symbol and the paint colours. The 'Trending' and 'Templates' still showing above the panel. The panel itself has no words at all.

first_pass.why: This panel has no heading and no words of any kind. The only marked box is the 'Trending' and 'Templates' row behind it, which belongs to the page underneath, not to the thing I am looking at. The symbols — four squares, a slanted block, a curved arrow — are not ones I know. If I looked away, I would have no idea what this panel was or how I came to it.
first_pass.solution: A heading at the top of the panel, such as 'Draw a picture', and words under each symbol ('Pen', 'Shapes', 'Rubber', 'Undo').

test_cases.action: Tap the three-line button, then 'Images', then the flower picture at the top left ('Sketch'). Say where you are. Swipe up once across the big white area. Say where you are now, and whether you are still on the same screen. Then tap the X at the top left of the panel and choose 'Discard' (that only throws away your own lines).
test_cases.real_if: it is real if you cannot say where you are on the panel, or if the swipe takes you somewhere else
test_cases.not_real_if: it is not real if you can name where you are before and after the swipe
test_cases.what_happened: With the 'Images' page scrolled right up, I tapped the flower picture 'Sketch'. A white panel came up over the bottom of the screen: a cross, a pencil, four squares, a slanted block, a curved arrow, a slider and some coloured dots. The panel itself has no name. Above it I could still see 'Images' and 'Trending'/'Templates', so I knew I was somewhere in the pictures section, but not what this panel was. I swiped up once across the white area. That did not take me anywhere: it drew a black line on the panel, and everything else stayed exactly where it was. So I was on the same screen before and after. When I tapped the cross, a box came up headed 'Discard sketch?'. Only then did the word 'sketch' tell me what the panel had been. I chose 'Discard' and was back on the 'Images' page.

s10.closing_comment: The drawing panel still has no name; I only learned it was a 'sketch' when the box asked me whether to discard it. At least 'Images' was showing above it.

s11.cue: The heading 'See yourself underwater' and the two buttons beneath it.

first_pass.why: The heading says in plain words what this panel is for, and the buttons are ordinary words. I would know what I was doing.

And it tells me something 'moved to Library' — I would not remember that by tomorrow.
first_pass.solution: A clear heading such as 'Make a picture' at the top, and the message shown somewhere it does not cover the controls.
